requestedActions.title: Read titles of work packages the connected person can access, including paginated results
Authorize access to the connected person's OpenProject account on their own instance via OAuth

guide.summary: OpenProject documents an OAuth2 authorization code flow whose default api_v3 scope acts on behalf of the current user. Reading work package titles relies on api_v3 plus the connected person's existing work package visibility, which bounds the results.
guide.recommendation: The requested API test is not ready yet. Resolve the access mapping for Read titles of work packages the connected person can access, including paginated results. Use “Find missing request” or add official documentation beside that action.

findings.title: Documented OAuth2 authorization code flow with auth and token endpoints
findings.detail: OpenProject lists Auth URL and Access Token URL endpoints for its OAuth2 server, uses an authorization code request with client ID, redirect URI and scope, and exchanges the code for a bearer access token and refresh token.
findings.appliesWhen: Customer connects their own OpenProject instance through the developer-owned OAuth application.

evidence.quote: Auth URL: https://example.com/oauth/authorize Access Token URL: https://example.com/oauth/token

https://example.com/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=<Client ID>&redirect_uri=<Redirect URI>&scope=<scope>&prompt=consent This requests redirects you to a URL that holds a code parameter which is the authentication code.
--data 'redirect_uri=<Redirect URI>' The response will look like this:

findings.title: api_v3 scope for the standard OpenProject API
findings.detail: Scopes are selected on the OAuth application; if no scope is checked, api_v3 is assumed. api_v3 is the standard OpenProject API, and the token performs calls on behalf of the current user.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies to the read of work packages through the standard API when the application requests the default api_v3 scope.

evidence.quote: Set the Scopes that the OAuth client application will be able to access. Multiple selection is possible. If no scope is checked, per default api_v3 is assumed. api_v3 is the
standard OpenProject API, while bcf_v2_1 is specific to the BIM edition of OpenProject.
With the token that you obtained above you can now make API calls to the OpenProject instance on behalf of the current user.

findings.title: Customer administrator registers the OAuth application on their instance
findings.detail: Administrators create and configure an OAuth app under Administration, set a redirect URL provided by the client app, and note the Client ID and Client secret. Confidential status applies to server-side clients.
findings.appliesWhen: Required once per customer instance before the customer authorizes access.

evidence.quote: - Create and configure an OAuth app
Press Create to add your OAuth application.
Tip Don’t forget to note down your Client ID and your Client secret in a safe space. You will need them later.

findings.title: Connected person must have work package visibility in the relevant projects
findings.detail: Work packages are returned only when the connected person has the View work packages permission in the project; otherwise the API returns a MissingPermission error. The OAuth grant does not add project visibility.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies when the connected person is expected to see work packages through their existing account role.

evidence.quote: View work packages – Allows users to view work packages.
"message" : "You are not allowed to see the work packages of this project."
Project-level: Permissions scoped to individual projects for users which are logged in - View work packages for users that are logged in Assign different permissions to the role Non-member

findings.title: Access token expires after two hours by default
findings.detail: The bearer token expires after two hours by default, after which the client must refresh or request a new token; the refresh token is returned with the initial token response.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies to paginated reads that run longer than the token lifetime or across later sessions.

evidence.quote: Please note that your Bearer token will expire after two hours (default) and you will have to click on “Request Token” again. Otherwise your API request will return an error
The response contains the bearer token (“access_token”) and a refresh token that you will need when working with the API. Please copy the tokens for reference.
"expires_in" : 7200 ,

steps.title: Register the OAuth application on the customer's OpenProject instance
steps.detail: The customer administrator creates an OAuth application under Administration > Authentication > OAuth applications, sets the redirect URL provided by the developer's client app, selects the api_v3 scope, and records the Client ID and Client secret. Confidential should be checked for a server-side client.
steps.doneWhen: Client ID and Client secret are recorded for use in the authorization and token steps; the application appears in the OAuth applications list.

evidence.quote: OAuth applications To configure OpenProject to act as a server to an OAuth client application, please navigate to Administration -> Authentication -> OAuth applications .
Tip Don’t forget to note down your Client ID and your Client secret in a safe space. You will need them later.
- Create and configure an OAuth app

fields: Client ID from the registered OAuth application
Client secret from the registered OAuth application
Redirect URL from the developer's client app

steps.title: Open the consent redirect and confirm the callback returns a code
steps.detail: The connected person opens the documented authorization URL on their instance, approves access, and is redirected to the registered redirect URI with a code parameter. Use the browser; this step is not executed by the agent.
steps.doneWhen: The callback URL contains a code parameter with the registered redirect URI.

evidence.quote: https://example.com/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=<Client ID>&redirect_uri=<Redirect URI>&scope=<scope>&prompt=consent This requests redirects you to a URL that holds a code parameter which is the authentication code.
Request authorization code Request an authorization code. Please adopt the following URL replacing:
In this example we skip that server side implementation and just copy the value of the code parameter from the URL that you see in your browser.

fields: CLIENT_ID from the registered OAuth application
REDIRECT_URI as configured on the OAuth application
INSTANCE_BASE_URL: your full HTTPS instance URL, without a trailing slash

steps.title: Exchange the authorization code for an access token
steps.detail: Exchange the code from the callback for a bearer access token and refresh token at the documented token URL using client_id and client_secret in the form body with grant_type authorization_code.
steps.doneWhen: The response contains access_token, refresh_token and expires_in.

evidence.quote: $ curl --request POST \
--data 'redirect_uri=<Redirect URI>' The response will look like this:
The response contains the bearer token (“access_token”) and a refresh token that you will need when working with the API. Please copy the tokens for reference.

fields: INSTANCE_BASE_URL: your full HTTPS instance URL, without a trailing slash
CLIENT_ID and CLIENT_SECRET from the registered application
AUTH_CODE from the callback URL
REDIRECT_URI matching the registered redirect
